newsitem.title: USA: Oxford Health, HMOs off on premium fears.
newsitem.headline: Oxford Health, HMOs off on premium fears.

text.p: Shares of Oxford Health Plans Inc and other health maintenance organizations continued to crumble on fears that the U.S. government would slow health maintenance organization premium growth rates, analysts said.
Oxford dropped three to 52-3/8, PacifiCare Health Systems Inc shed 2-1/6 to 72-1/4 and United Healthcare Corp fell one to 43-1/4, furthering Monday's losses.
"It's a complete overreaction to news the market dosen't understand," said Roberta Walter, an analyst with Goldman Sachs.

Reports that the White House was considering substantial cuts in premiums Medicare pays to HMOs sparked a two-day selloff in HMO stocks. If adopted, the reductions could trim about $20 billion from HMO premiums over the next five years.
But analysts said the cuts would have a negligible effect on HMOs' earnings. In recent years, the growth in Medicare premiums has been greater than HMOs needed to provide care, some analysts said.
"The premium growth rates would slow to levels analysts already expect and have built into earnings estimates," Walter said.
If premium growth rates shrank, HMOs would initiate other measures -- such as surcharges -- to maintain revenues and earnings, said one analyst, who declined to be named.
